# Settings reference

Every setting, by area. Each row says where the control is, which scopes it has, what it does and costs, and its effective default: what
an untouched install does. Rarely changed settings sit under their section's **Advanced** fold. What each part costs in model calls and
waiting: [Costs and waiting](README.md#costs-and-waiting).

## Where settings live

Open **Extensions → Story Orchestrator → Open Story Orchestrator**. The window has two halves: **This story** (Play, Features, Review,
Author) for the chat that is open, and **Orchestrator** (Library, Defaults, Connections, Interface, Help) for the whole install. The route
icon in SillyTavern's top bar opens **This story → Play**.

| Scope | What it holds | Where you change it |
|---|---|---|
| Install | Model connections, the judge, images, and every feature's default | **Orchestrator → Connections**, **Orchestrator → Defaults** |
| Story | What the story's author chose for a feature (on, off or tuned) | The story itself, in the Studio |
| Chat | Your change to a feature for this chat only | **This story → Features** |
| Device | Display and animation preferences, kept in this browser for your SillyTavern account | **Orchestrator → Interface → This device** |

A feature uses the first of: this chat's change, the story's choice, the install default. An install default switched off is a master
switch: no story or chat can turn that feature back on. A device preference changes only how this browser shows things.

Worked example: **Speaker direction** is on in **Orchestrator → Defaults**. A story turns it off for its own chats. In one of those chats
you open **This story → Features → Speaker direction** and switch it on: that chat now uses it, the story's other chats do not, and the
feature page says this chat re-enables something the story turned off. **Reset to story/default** on the same page drops your change, and
the chat follows the story again.

In the tables, **Scope** says which of these a row can be set at, and **Where** names the install control first, then the chat or device one.

## Memory

The memory model that reads the chat, and what the story remembers. [More](../setup/memory-model.md)

| Setting | Where | Scope | What it does | Default | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Let the story move forward on its own** | Orchestrator → Defaults → Story reading; this chat: This story → Features → Story reading | Install, story, chat | After replies, a second model reads the chat and moves the story on when what it needs has happened. Leave it on unless you want to move the story by hand. Costs one call to the memory model every few messages. | On | `extraction.enabled` |
| **Memory model** | Orchestrator → Connections → Memory → Memory model | Install | The Connection Manager profile that reads the chat after replies to track the story and remember what happened. It does not replace your chat model. Pick a fast, cheap model; every chat uses this choice. | Not set | `extraction.profileId` |
| **Fallback when it is down** | Orchestrator → Connections → Memory → Memory model | Install | When the memory model stops answering, its work goes to this profile until it answers again; it is checked every few minutes and switched back on its own. Leave it empty and the work waits for the memory model. | None | `extraction.fallbackProfileId` |
| **Reply thinking** | Orchestrator → Defaults → Reply thinking; this chat: This story → Features → Reply thinking | Install, story, chat | How long your chat model may think before each reply in a story chat. Medium is a good default: as clean as no limit, and replies start sooner. Only applies to llama.cpp setups that think; other backends are left alone. | Medium | `extraction.replyEffort` |
| **Read the chat every … messages** | Orchestrator → Defaults → Story reading; this chat: This story → Features → Story reading | Install, story, chat | How often the memory model reads the chat. Lower reacts faster but calls the memory model more often; higher saves calls and reacts later. | 3 | `extraction.cadence` |
| **Wait before reading the newest messages** | Orchestrator → Defaults → Story reading; this chat: This story → Features → Story reading | Install, story, chat | Leave the newest messages out of a read, in case you often re-roll them. 0 reacts to the newest message straight away; re-rolls are undone either way. | 0 | `extraction.stabilityLag` |
| **Model for this task** | Orchestrator → Connections → Memory → Models per task | Install | Send this task to a different Connection Manager profile than the memory model, for example a faster model for frequent work or a stronger one for summaries. Left on "Same as memory model", it uses the memory model; the wizard's task uses opencode gpt-6.1-sol when the harness plugin offers it, else a DeepSeek profile when there is one. Claude Code claude-sonnet-5-5 is the other wizard route. | Same as memory model | `extraction.profiles` |
| **Story read line order** | Orchestrator → Connections → Memory → Memory model | Install | A measurement arm: the story read lists its fixed instructions first and the lines that change from read to read (the current scene, what happened, open threads and promises, known names, the questions) after them, so a local server can reuse the start of each read. The same lines in a new order. Off, today's order, until a live test on the GPU shows the read scores within 0.02 of today's: an exception to every feature being on by default. No control yet: a measurement run switches it on. | Off (today's order) | `extraction.readLayout` |
| **Thinking for this task** | Orchestrator → Connections → Memory → Models per task | Install | How long the model may think on this task. Default sends nothing extra; higher can be more careful and costs time and tokens. | Per entry | `extraction.routes.*.route.options.effort` |
| **If the harness fails** | Orchestrator → Connections → Memory → Models per task | Install | What happens when the harness cannot answer: pause this task, or send it to a Connection Manager profile instead. | Per entry | `extraction.routes.*.onFailure.profileId` |

| **Write a record when a chapter ends** | Orchestrator → Defaults → Chapters and long-chat context; this chat: This story → Features → Chapters and long-chat context | Install, story, chat | For stories that declare chapters: when a chapter ends, its memories are written up as one record. | **Add the story so far to every prompt** | Orchestrator → Defaults → Chapters and long-chat context; this chat: This story → Features → Chapters and long-chat context | Install, story, chat | The chapter records ride every prompt as a fixed-size story so far, so long stories keep their past. This switch covers only that continuity check. The other reply checks (your part, house rules, attention, voice, ideas) share the same warden call under their own judge use switches, so warden calls can still appear with this off. | **Notes about the player's part** | Orchestrator → Defaults → Player agency; this chat: This story → Features → Player agency | Install, story, chat | When a reply writes what only you do, say or decide, or ignores what you just said, the next reply's prompt carries a one-line reminder. Only replies are checked; your own messages are never changed. | `auto` | `stagecraft.agencyAcceptMode` |

## World

How a story's lorebooks are switched on, and the lorebook helper. [More](../setup/README.md#story-lorebooks)

| **Memory text can trigger lore** | Orchestrator → Defaults → Memory-triggered lore; this chat: This story → Features → Memory-triggered lore | Install, story, chat | Established facts, scene history and the current guidance join every lorebook scan, so an entry whose keys they mention can activate. | **Per-turn lore after the history** | Orchestrator → Defaults → Late lore placement; this chat: This story → Features → Late lore placement | Install, story, chat | Story lorebook entries that come and go turn by turn (keyword and lore-select picks) are placed a few messages from the end of the chat instead of beside the character card. ## Images

Optional pictures and character sprites; both need your own image setup. [More](../setup/images.md)

| Setting | Where | Scope | What it does | Default | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Allow automatic illustrations on this install** | Orchestrator → Defaults → Illustrations; this chat: This story → Features → Illustrations | Install, story, chat | Lets stories and the automation below draw pictures through SillyTavern’s configured image backend. ## Judge

An optional fast model for small choices; it never blocks a reply. [More](../setup/judge.md)

| Setting | Where | Scope | What it does | Default | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Use the judge** | Orchestrator → Connections → Judge | Install | A second, fast model for yes/no and pick-one decisions. Each use can be switched off on its own and says what it sends. It never receives character cards, persona text, other chats or the key. | On | `judge.enabled` |
| **Judge uses** | Orchestrator → Connections → Judge | Install | Each use answers one kind of question for the story. Switch off any you do not want; the story falls back to its usual path. | Per entry | `judge.uses` |
| **Where this use runs** | Orchestrator → Connections → Judge | Install | Which provider answers this use. A provider that was not measured for a use is refused, and the use takes its usual path. The attention and voice checks share the warden's call, so they take the warden's provider and have none of their own. | Per entry | `judge.provider` |

## Authoring

Tools for writing stories. [More, for authors](../author/README.md) (in the in-app guide, author pages show only in Author view)

| Setting | Where | Scope | What it does | Default | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Enable the wizard** | Orchestrator → Library → Start → New story | Install | Turns on the story wizard in the Studio and the author's suggestion tools. It uses your authoring model and costs calls only while you use it. | On | `copilot.enabled` |
| **Outlines per gap** | Orchestrator → Connections → Judge → Outlines for the road ahead | Install | Write this many outlines for each gap in the story and keep the best one. Each extra outline is another run of the story model. | 1 | `judge.expansion.variants` |
| **Best outline picked by** | Orchestrator → Connections → Judge → Outlines for the road ahead | Install | Who picks the best outline: the judge's score, or the story model. | `code` | `judge.expansion.pick` |

## Setup

What SillyTavern features were found, and a copy for a bug report. [More](../setup/README.md)

| Setting | Where | Scope | What it does | Default | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Ask questions** | Orchestrator → Help → Setup → Ask questions | Install | Ask in Help, the wizard or /story ask. It only reads; while you play it knows only what you have seen. A few model calls per question. | On | `copilot.ask` |

## Experiments

Trials that are not measured yet. Each is on by default so it is seen in play; none has a control in the window. To switch one off, set
its key to `false` in the extension's stored settings (`spikes` inside `extension_settings["story-orchestrator"].settings`) and reload.

| Experiment | What it does | Default | Key |
|---|---|---|---|
| swipeBackCache | Swiping back to a reply you saw before restores the story state that reply had, instead of reading it again. | On | `spikes.swipeBackCache` |
| sp6Complications | In a story that declares complications, one is added to the prompt after a few of your turns pass without the scene changing. | On | `spikes.sp6Complications` |
| reasoningEffect | Lets a scene set its own reply thinking budget, over the install's Reply thinking. | On | `spikes.reasoningEffect` |
| editReread | After you edit the last reply, your next reply waits until the edit has been read, up to 15 seconds. | On | `spikes.editReread` |
| thoughtCarry | When no private intent is ready for a character, a short aim from that character's own last thought stands in. | On | `spikes.thoughtCarry` |
